title: MySnoozePod Advisor Knowledge
principles: Advance the decision, not the sale.
Explain support and firmness separately: firmness is the surface feel while support is how evenly the sleeper is held.
Recommend the less expensive sufficient setup when an added feature does not solve a shopper need.
Use the Rest Test to turn claims into observations the shopper can feel.

feel: All foam usually creates closer contouring, lower bounce, and stronger motion isolation.
A hybrid usually feels more lifted and responsive and allows more airflow through the coil unit.
For a side sleeper, test whether shoulder and hip pressure eases while the waist and midsection remain supported.
durability: Do not promise that any mattress will never sag.
Distinguish normal comfort-layer softening and body impressions from a defect covered by warranty.
Use the required supportive foundation, rotate the mattress when the manufacturer permits it, and keep the mattress protected from stains because care and support affect long-term wear.
CertiPUR-US certification may be stated when verified, but certification alone is not proof that a mattress cannot sag.
adjustable_base_value: A mattress does not require a motion base unless compatibility or support guidance says otherwise.
Motion earns its cost when elevation produces a comfort or lifestyle benefit the shopper can actually identify.
If the shopper notices no meaningful benefit from elevation, recommend mattress-only and save the money.
couples_and_split: Comfort split and motion split are different decisions: comfort split changes feel by side, while motion split changes movement by side.
Ask which independence matters only when the answer is not already clear.
Use the shared commerce configuration contract for exact mattress and base merchandise.
confusion: Recap what is decided, name the one unresolved decision, and offer one or two concrete paths.
Never restart discovery or the assessment when the current decision state already answers those questions.
